result.note: Tests FSSAI's August 2026 front-of-pack labelling proposal: its two-nutrient trigger, the exemption, and how it compares with labelling systems abroad.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) proposed warning labels for packaged food and drinks in a filing before the Supreme Court. Consider the following statements about the proposal:
items: A warning would apply to any product high in just one of saturated fat, sugar or salt.
Single-ingredient foods are exempt from the proposed labelling.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the red hexagon applies only to products high in two or more of saturated fat, sugar or salt. Single-ingredient foods are exempt, and the rollout is phased. The Supreme Court had floated a one-nutrient trigger, so a drink high only in sugar escapes the warning under FSSAI's version.
questions.source: In a Supreme Court filing on Friday, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) called for a red hexagon on products high in two or more of saturated fat, sugar, or salt.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs of jurisdictions and front-of-pack food labelling systems:
items: India (FSSAI proposal, August 2026) — Red hexagon warning
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: All three are correctly matched: the UK uses traffic-light ratings, Nutri-Score is used across Europe, and FSSAI proposed a red hexagon for India. Industry groups that opposed labels in India as confusing use such systems abroad.
questions.source: Coca-Cola, Nestle, and PepsiCo industry groups have long opposed labels as confusing, though many use them abroad, from traffic-light ratings in the UK to Nutri-Score across Europe.
